responsibility: `rustc_attr` is the compiler’s central utility crate for understanding and enforcing Rust attributes, especially builtin attributes, so later compiler stages can rely on a validated, structured view of attribute metadata. Its crate root (`lib.rs`) defines this role by wiring together builtin-attribute handling and attribute-specific diagnostics, re-exporting the main parsing and representation APIs, and loading the crate’s fluent diagnostic messages. The builtin-attribute implementation in `builtin.rs` provides the core attribute data types and the logic to parse, classify, and validate builtin attributes such as stability and const-stability markers, representation hints, inlining and optimization controls, instruction-set annotations, and macro transparency, including checking arguments and enforcing builtin-specific rules. The diagnostic layer in `session_diagnostics.rs` defines the structured errors, labels, codes, and suggestions used when those attributes are malformed or invalid. Together, these files make `rustc_attr` the part of rustc that turns raw attribute syntax into compiler-usable attribute semantics and reports attribute misuse consistently.
